Hi Soojin / Ben — thanks for the demo earlier. Two quick items from our side related to compliance:  

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report for the inference platform (or a scoped report that covers hosted inference)? If you don’t have the report, would a bridge/interim attestation suffice for our procurement timeline?  
2) We’ll need temporary access to your evidence vault (SecureVault or equivalent) so our security team can validate a handful of controls (access logs, change management, encryption at rest). Ideally we can get read-only access for two users (myself and our legal lead Daniel).

We’re aiming to close procurement by end of month, so if you can share a recommended path (report + bridge letter + portal invite) that maps to a 1–2 week turnaround, that’d be great.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Hannah — great to connect today, appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:  

- Yes, Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report that covers our hosted API and core inference runtime. Standard report is our audited period through Mar 31, 2028.
- We can provide a formal Type II report (PDF) plus a short bridge/interim attestation letter that calls out any changes since the report period and confirms no material control changes. That combo usually satisfies procurement teams.
- We’ll send a SecureVault invite for read-only view for you and Daniel. The invite will include the audit report, the bridge letter draft, and a targeted evidence packet (access logs sampling, key rotation records, and change-control excerpts).

Next steps I propose (timeline in parentheses):
1) Internal kickoff to assemble artifacts and draft bridge letter (Ben + Karthik) — today (same day).
2) Share bridge letter draft + SecureVault invite (1 business day).
3) Novapulse reviews and signals any follow-up evidence requests (1–3 business days).

I’m looping in Ben and Karthik to coordinate artifact pull and to own the bridge letter draft.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that sounds good and aligns with our timeline. A few quick legal/procurement items:  

1) The bridge letter should explicitly state the scope (hosted API + inference runtime) and the audited period end date. Please include a short note about data residency guarantees for US customers.
2) For SecureVault access, we prefer SSO with SAML at the invite stage if possible; if not, a one-time link with read-only credentials is fine.  
3) Can you include a single-page summary that maps each control we’ll likely review (e.g., Logical Access, Change Management, Backup/Recovery) to the artifact we’re provided? That'll speed our internal review.

If you can get the SecureVault invite and bridge letter draft by EOD tomorrow PDT, procurement will be able to include Redwood in the next procurement sprint.

—Daniel
